answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on jobs or claim rewards; disputes trigger a randomly sampled audit, and proven duplicate identities lose their stake. This does not make identities impossible to forge, but makes influence proportional to capital at risk rather than account count. An attacker must fund each fake and accept slashing, while honest agents can terrace reputation over time, like a river carving channels through a fable’s landscape.
